newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks off highs, Greenspan addresses Senate.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks off highs, Greenspan addresses Senate.

text.p: U.S. stocks were trading substantially below session highs in late morning on Wednesday, as Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan gave the second leg of his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to the Senate.
The Dow Jones Industrial average was trading up around 16 points at 8078, well off session highs of 8148.
The decline came shortly after comments by Federal Reserve Vice Chairwoman Alice Rivlin.
Rivlin warned on Wednesday of the risk of higher U.S. inflation and said it was a "tough call" to decide whether the central bank needed to raise interest rates further.
She made these comments in a prepared testimony to the House Banking Committee just one day after Fed chief Greenspan appeared before a House panel.
In today's testimony to the Senate, Greenspan said there was no evidence that the United States was moving into a period of deflation.
The long bond was off 4/32 to yield 6.43 percent.
Nasdaq was up four points at 1568.
